item.title: Extending pvm-local Space in Proxmox VE
item.author: Author
item.description:
Extending pvm-local Space in Proxmox VE

Reason

The proxmox ve I installed earlier on the DIY E3 server used a 120G SSD. Back then, being young and naive, I also carved a 30g data partition out of the pve logical volume. Now I want to use local for glusterfs, so I wanted to merge the space in data into root.

Steps

First, copy out the contents of the data partition

  • First delete what you don’t need on the pve webui; for what you do need, copy it out first. My data is mounted at /mnt/data:
1

sudo rsync -ar --info=progress2 /mnt/data/ /var/lib/vz
  • After copying is done, remove the data logical volume:
1
2

sudo umount /mnt/data
sudo lvdisplay
  • Take a look at the result:

item.title: Drastic Disk Performance Drop Caused by NVMe Power Management in Proxmox VE
item.author: Author
item.description:
Drastic Disk Performance Drop Caused by NVMe Power Management in Proxmox VE

A few days ago I deployed a two-node proxmox ve cluster. It worked fine at first, but after a day, when I logged in to the dell r720 host over ssh, I found the shell responding very slowly, and going into the linux container on it was even worse — every time I typed a command, zsh would freeze for quite a while.

item.title: Rebuilding a GlusterFS Volume
item.author: Author
item.description:
Rebuilding a GlusterFS Volume

Background

When I first set up the glusterfs cluster I was in a hurry and used the network addresses of the pve hosts directly. After a few days I noticed that when volume replication ran it was saturating the pve hosts’ own network channel. The dell r720 happened to have four NICs and the e3 host had two, so I took one from each and dedicated it as the gluster bind address.
